$comment: Settings of pipeline:river-lines (WP 5.1): each approved river's course assembled from the display lines (APRHI inside the province, IGN outside; precedence APRHI > IGN > HydroRIVERS, owner). Values set from the WP 5.0a/5.0b measurements (2026-10-13): line endpoints of different lines either meet within 1 m (22.6% of endpoints) or lie 50 m or more apart (only 2.4% fall between 1 and 50 m), so snapM 50 joins clean junctions without merging separate lines; the own lines of one river can stop short of each other: R. Quinto (Popopis) lines meet within 0-600 m (WP 5.0a), so extensionGapM is 600; a line that leaves another mid-piece is covered by attachM instead. snapM: line endpoints within this distance (m) are one junction (the graph node). corridorM: candidate pieces are limited to the river's own root(s) (a river's course never leaves them); within them, the drawn pieces within this distance (m) of the river's HydroRIVERS reaches (South America Albers), plus every piece that carries the river's own name wherever it lies; the anchors must also lie within it of the reaches. gapSearchM: a virtual gap edge may join two dangling line ends (a node with one piece, or one touching another river's course) of different connected pieces up to this far apart (m); gaps on a course are recorded in gaps.json and never filled. gapNeighbours: each dangling end gets virtual edges to at most this many nearest ends of other components (bounds the graph; added by the builder, not in the brief). Besides those, every pair of components within gapSearchM is joined once between their closest nodes (any node, loops included), so a path exists whenever the lines are chained within gapSearchM. weights: cost per metre of a piece on the cheapest source-to-mouth path: own = a piece named as the river (name or alias, a parenthesised alias in the piece name is ignored), unnamed = a piece with no name (APRHI starred names count as unnamed), other = a piece named otherwise; gap = per metre of straight virtual edge. A path prefers own pieces, bridges over unnamed ones, and uses another river's name only when nothing else connects. excludeClasses: piece classes (APRHI Clase or IGN class, case and accent insensitive) never used on a course, for channels that carry no water: APRHI TIPO 'Paleocauce' (relict channel, 20 lines, 78.6 km). Neither APRHI nor IGN has a canal class; APRHI SISTEMATIZ 'SI' is not used because it includes main rivers (R. Quinto 115.9 km, R. Jesús María 150 km); the meaning of both values is unverified until APRHI's metadata is read (PENDING.md). mouthLakeIds: lakes (lakes.parquet ids) a course that ends at them is extended to: from the mouth it follows own-named pieces to the one with an endpoint closest to the lake ('aprhi-nat-1582' is Mar Chiquita; the own lines of Primero, Jesús María and Dulce end 0-0.44 km from it, measured in WP 5.0b). lakeTouchM: an endpoint within this distance (m) of a mouth lake touches it. anchorMaxM: the source and mouth anchors (where the course starts and ends) take the nearest line junction that touches a piece named as the river, within this distance (m) of the upstream end of the most upstream HydroRIVERS reach / the downstream end of the mouth reach; failing that, the nearest junction with a real piece. The report says which rule chose each anchor and checks both anchors are within this distance (the 15″ paths can end kilometres from the mapped channel). extensionGapM: the own-named extensions (mouth to a lake's shore, source up the river) may cross a break of up to this length (m) between the ends of two own-named lines that no chain of own-named pieces joins (beyond snapM); each break is recorded as a gap of kind 'extension' in gaps.json. A mouth extension still has to reach within lakeTouchM of a mouthLakeIds lake. When the mouth anchor itself cannot reach the lake, the extension may start from another node of the course, which then ends the course there. After the course and the claims, every unclaimed own-named piece joined to the course through own-named pieces only is added as an 'arm' (owner, 2026-10-13: tramos that follow the river's channel are part of the river); arms are not counted in the course km. attachM: a line end within this distance (m) of the interior of another piece attaches to it there, without splitting the piece (course.parquet keeps whole pieces; the attachment only adds connectivity). Own-named line ends attach to this river's course: as an arm, or, for the mouth extension, as the continuation (the course then ends at the attached piece's downstream end). A line end that attaches to the interior of a piece an earlier river holds ends the river's course there (a confluence). Every attachment is recorded in gaps.json (kind 'attach', with the distance). Evidence: R. Jesús María's lower arm aprhi:826:2#0 starts 100.5 m from the interior of its main line's piece aprhi:826:0#20 (5 km long), 1,327.5 m from the nearest piece end; attachM 500 is the same distance as the confluence search used for other rivers. Rivers are processed receivers first (the river a mouth flows into is processed before the rivers that flow into it), so a tributary finds the receiver's pieces already held. ownShareTarget: a check that only warns until the settings are calibrated; a river's course should hold at least this share of the own-named km among its candidates. WP 5.2 (2026-10-13) gap fill: every path gap of a course gets one fill piece (fill.parquet), and so does the break between a river's course and its receiver's when no line joins them. IGN first (owner exception to R3.3: the raw IGN lines, perennial and intermittent as in lines.config.json, inside the province too, but only in gaps): the cheapest chain of IGN line parts (length times the weights above) from a line end within fillSnapM of the gap's upstream end to one within fillSnapM of its downstream end; a line passing a gap end is cut there. Otherwise the river's HydroRIVERS reaches between the ends, cut at the points nearest them, with straight connectors to the exact ends (counted as hydrorivers km); where that route is not credible (see fillMaxStretch) the fill is the straight line between the exact ends, traced to the nearest reaches, and counted as hydrorivers km too (form 'connector' in fill.parquet and the report; its sourceIds are the nearest reaches, not the source of the geometry). fillCorridorM: IGN line parts are offered only within this distance (m) of the gap's guide (the HydroRIVERS route and the straight line between the ends). Measured on the 85 fills of the 2026-10-13 run: the IGN fills (31 pieces, 42.6 km) are identical for 100 to 2000 m, 50 m loses 0.47 km, and at 3000 to 5000 m a Conlara chain of 21.7 km joins a 1.57 km gap (stretch 14.3); 500 m is five times the smallest sufficient value and keeps that detour out. fillSnapM: an IGN line end within this distance (m) of a gap end, or of another IGN line end, is one junction; the fill's ends lie at most this far from the gap's ends (the check noGapLeft). IGN km filled with 50 / 100 / 150 / 250 / 500 m: 41.0 / 42.6 / 43.0 / 41.0 / 38.0; 100 m is twice snapM and the largest end offset measured with it was 92.3 m. fillMaxStretch: an IGN chain or a HydroRIVERS route is used only if no longer than this times the straight distance between the gap ends plus 2 * fillSnapM, else it is a detour and the next source is tried. Measured: the accepted IGN chains reach a stretch of 1.81 at most, the rejected one is 14.3 (Conlara); of the 53 HydroRIVERS fills of gaps, 18 are routes and 35 straight lines, because on the plains the 15″ path strays from the channel (Dulce: a 17.1 km route for a 0.84 km gap; Saladillo: 10.5 km for 0.56 km). armMaxFromCourseM: an arm piece farther than this (m) from the course (pieces and fill) is not part of the river. Distances measured (the report lists the five farthest per river): Quinto 28,649 m (the Popopis lower branch, aprhi:3996:0#26 to #36), Pichanas 16,240, Jesús María 4,845, Conlara 2,893, Salí 1,156, Dulce 914, the rest 0; 30,000 keeps all of them and bounds a chain of own-named breaks.
